**Finding: missing (high severity) — Termination for convenience (T4C)**

- **What we found:** Section 9 contains only for-cause termination rights (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Vendor security/service/law/IP failures) plus 9.5's cumulative-remedies statement. No convenience right exists anywhere for either Party. The term is three years (8.1), and Section 2.1 locks in a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights." Section 8.2 (non-renewal) and Section 27.3 (force-majeure exit) are partial exits and not substitutes.
- **Why it fails:** Under the rule, absence of a Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation, and no right at all in a multi-year commitment is walk-away territory.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** New Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form, in whole or in part, with a refund of prepaid Fees and no early-termination fee, expressly notwithstanding Section 2.1, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a term. Fallback of 60 days' notice offered in the comment. No Vendor convenience right needed deleting.
